text: An equilibrium is 'hyperbolic', so Hartman-Grobman applies, precisely when:
choices: all eigenvalues of the linearization are real and distinct
no eigenvalue of the linearization lies on the imaginary axis
explanation: Hyperbolicity means no eigenvalue has zero real part (none on the imaginary axis), so the flow is topologically conjugate to its linearization. Eigenvalues need not be real; hyperbolic points include unstable saddles; a zero determinant would actually violate hyperbolicity.
